title: Functional Options
hints: An `Option` is just a function that edits a `*Server`. Each `WithX` returns a closure that remembers its argument: `func WithName(name string) Option { return func(s *Server) { s.name = name } }`. `WithMiddleware` uses `append(s.middleware, names...)`.

`New`: build `s := &Server{addr: addr, name: DefaultName, timeout: DefaultTimeout, maxConns: DefaultMaxConns}`, run `for _, opt := range opts { opt(s) }`, then collect problems in `var errs []error` and `return nil, err` when `err := errors.Join(errs...)` is non-nil (`Join` of nothing is `nil`).

`String` is `fmt.Sprintf("%s@%s timeout=%v maxConns=%d middleware=%v", …)`; a nil `[]string` prints as `[]`. `Middleware` returns `slices.Clone(s.middleware)`. `NewProduction` builds `opts := []server.Option{server.WithName("api"), …}` and calls `server.New(addr, append(opts, extra...)...)`.
